patients.summary: Office administrator with hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide and known hereditary angioedema who joined in 2018. Practice care 2018 to mid-2023 covers cervical radiculopathy, an open cholecystectomy, an HAE attack and a right vestibular schwannoma treated with radiosurgery; after she was last seen in June 2023, outside records bring a resected pheochromocytoma, atrial flutter, a left midbrain stroke and HCTZ-related pancreatitis.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

43 y/o woman, office administrator, transferring care from her prior primary care office (records release signed today). Main reasons for switching: access, and wanting someone who knows what HAE is.

HTN: on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg every morning for about four years, started by the prior PCP. Home cuff readings mostly 120s/high 70s. No side effects she notices. No headaches, chest pain, swelling.

Hereditary angioedema: her mother has confirmed C1 inhibitor deficiency and the patient was told she has the same thing. Swelling episodes since she was a small child: lips, hands or feet, occasionally genital swelling, and bouts of bad crampy belly pain. Each one runs 2-3 days and goes away by itself. Antihistamines were tried years ago and did nothing. Has never been given anything specific for it and does not carry any rescue medicine. No throat involvement she can remember. Last bad episode was over a year ago.

PMH: as above. No surgeries.
Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily.
Allergies: none to drugs, none to foods.
FH: mother HAE (C1-INH deficiency). Father with high blood pressure, had a stroke at 60.
SH: never smoker. A drink or two a month. Works full time in an office.

ROS otherwise negative.

EXAM
Vitals per flowsheet. Comfortable, well appearing.
HEENT: no lip or tongue swelling, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement.
CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender, no masses.
Ext: no edema, no swelling of hands or feet.
Skin: no rash or urticaria.
Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions; Pap/HPV collected.
Neuro: grossly nonfocal.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Essential hypertension, controlled on HCTZ 25. Continue. CMP today.
2. Hereditary angioedema, C1-INH deficiency by family history and her report. Not on any HAE therapy. She is not interested in a specialist right now since attacks are infrequent. Reminded her that ACE inhibitors and estrogen-containing products should be avoided. Will revisit.
3. Health maintenance: Pap with HPV collected. Screening mammogram ordered. CBC, lipids, TSH, A1c. Offered one-time HIV and hep C screening, she agreed. Colon screening starts at 45.
4. Prior records requested.

Return after labs/records, BP check in about six months.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap test and HPV test are both negative. With a normal co-test we repeat in five years.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jennifer, everything from yesterday came back fine. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the water pill, blood counts are normal, thyroid and A1c are normal, cholesterol is acceptable, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Pap results usually take a week or so; I'll send those when they're in.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great thank you! I called about the mammogram and they can take me in November.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received 41 pages from patient's former primary care practice (2012-2018). Includes: office notes; BP log; hydrochlorothiazide started 2014 for elevated readings on several visits; Pap smear 2016 negative; screening mammogram 2017 negative (BI-RADS 1); routine labs 2017 unremarkable. Problem list there: hypertension, hereditary angioedema (by family history). No HAE complement testing found in these records. Scanned to Media tab.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here before work for her flu shot. Screening questions negative, no egg or vaccine reactions in the past. Quadrivalent flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 min, no issues.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: 2017 outside study. Breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

documents.title: Mammogram result letter
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dear Ms. Kaminski, your screening mammogram on 11/07/2018 showed no evidence of cancer. Your breast tissue is heterogeneously dense; this is common and is noted for your information. We recommend continued yearly screening.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: HCTZ 25 mg, last fill from old prescriber, no refills left. Per PCP, new Rx sent for 90 days with 3 refills. Pt notified by voicemail.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP recheck. Taking HCTZ every morning, misses maybe once a month. Home readings 118-130 over 74-82. One minor lip swelling episode around New Year's that lasted two days, nothing in the belly, no throat symptoms.

Exam: BP as charted, at goal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No ankle swelling.

A/P:
HTN - at goal on HCTZ 25. BMP for potassium/sodium today.
HAE - mild facial episode, self-limited. Brought up seeing allergy/immunology for a rescue medication; she would rather hold off for now, it's been tolerable. Will keep offering.

See me for a physical in late summer.

documents.title: BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium and potassium normal on HCTZ, creatinine normal. Message sent.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 44F.

Interval: feels well. BP fine at home. Two short swelling episodes this year, one hand, one lip, both gone in a couple of days without treatment. No abdominal attacks.

Meds: HCTZ 25 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: unchanged, never smoked, rare alcohol. Walks at lunch most days.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. Well appearing. Ears and throat normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, nipple discharge or skin change; axillae negative. Abdomen soft. Extremities without edema. Skin without suspicious lesions.

Plan:
- HTN controlled. Continue HCTZ.
- HAE stable, infrequent attacks. Again offered allergy referral for an on-demand drug, declined for now.
- Tdap today (last tetanus she can't recall, over 10 years).
- Mammogram due November, ordered.
- Pap/HPV negative 2018, next 2023.
- Fasting labs today.
- Flu shot in October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jennifer, labs from Thursday are fine: normal blood count, kidney function, electrolytes and sugar, and cholesterol about where it was last year. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Lunch-hour flu shot. No illness today. Quadrivalent influenza 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, lot recorded in the immunization record. Tolerated well.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis compared with 2018 and 2017. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new mass, suspicious calcification or distortion. Stable appearance.

documents.title: Mammogram result letter
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Your mammogram of 11/13/2019 was normal (BI-RADS 1). Next screening in one year.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Office converting routine in-person follow-ups during the COVID closure. Patient prefers to wait a few weeks and do a video visit. Cancelled 3/24, will call her back to schedule video.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, she is at her kitchen table, working from home since March. Consent for telehealth given.

BP: home cuff log over two weeks, 116-128 systolic, 72-80 diastolic. Taking HCTZ daily. No lightheadedness.
HAE: no episodes since the fall.
Otherwise doing OK with the shutdown, sleeping fine, mood good.

Observed on video: comfortable, no facial swelling, speaking full sentences.

A/P: HTN well controlled on home readings, continue HCTZ 25. Turns 45 this week: discussed colon screening options, she chose a FIT kit by mail. In-person physical in September with labs.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat yearly. Released to portal with a note.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, masked visit.

45F, still mostly remote for work. Feels fine. HTN: home BPs remain in range. HAE: one belly episode in July, cramping and bloating for two days, rode it out at home with fluids. No airway symptoms ever.
PHQ-2: 1 (some low days with the isolation, not most days).

Exam: vitals as noted. Pleasant, in no distress. HEENT normal, no lip or tongue swelling. Neck without nodes. Heart regular rate, no murmurs or gallops. Lungs clear to auscultation. Breast exam deferred to mammogram per her preference. Abdomen soft, non-tender. No peripheral edema.

A/P
- HTN at goal: HCTZ 25 mg.
- HAE: an abdominal attack this summer. Talked again about having something on hand for attacks and about seeing allergy/immunology. She'll think about it; she doesn't love the idea of injections.
- Flu vaccine given today.
- Mammogram ordered. FIT in the spring was negative; next kit next year.
- Labs today.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP, CBC, lipids all within normal range. Released with comment.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Compared with 2019 and 2018. Heterogeneously dense. No suspicious findings. No change.

documents.title: Mammogram result letter
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Your screening mammogram on 11/18/2020 was normal. Please schedule next year's mammogram in November.
